record.field: Build a 30-second business briefing for a partner from their record and recent chatter.

# Partner Brief
Produce a short business briefing the user can read in 30 seconds for a single partner record:
1. Resolve the target partner: model `res.partner` + id (or pinned record from `<ui_ctx>`). If still missing, call `ask_user` once. 2. Use `read_records` to fetch the partner. Limit `fields` to the user-meaningful set: `name`, `is_company`, `email`, `phone`, `country_id`, `city`, `industry_id`, `customer_rank`, `supplier_rank`, `category_id`, `user_id`, `parent_id`. 3. Use `search_read` on `mail.message` with domain `[('model','=','res.partner'),('res_id','=',<id>), ('message_type','in',['comment','email'])]`, order `date desc`, limit 5, fields `author_id,date,subject,body`. 4. Output: - Header: `Display Name (res.partner,<id>) — Company / Contact` - 5-7 key/value bullets (label · value), skipping empties. - "Recent activity" line listing the 3 most recent log dates + short subject. - One-line relationship summary: customer / supplier / both / prospect, plus the salesperson if set. 5. Stop. Do not propose actions unless asked.
Draft a short follow-up message to a partner using their last interactions for context.

# Draft Follow-up
Draft a tactful follow-up message to a partner. Do not send anything; return the draft for the user to review:
1. Resolve the target partner (model `res.partner` + id or pinned record). If missing, `ask_user` once. 2. Use `search_read` on `mail.message` with domain `[('model','=','res.partner'),('res_id','=',<id>), ('message_type','in',['comment','email'])]`, order `date desc`, limit 3, fields `date,subject,body,author_id`. This grounds the follow-up in real prior context. 3. Compose a draft: - Tone: warm, professional, plain prose. - Length cap: 90 words. - Reference the most recent prior interaction concretely (date + topic). If there is none, open with a soft re-introduction. - End with a single, low-friction next step (a question or a proposed slot), not a hard ask. 4. Output the draft as a plain message, no preamble. After the draft, one short line listing the prior messages you used. Stop.
Walk a single record's important fields in plain language.

# Explain a Record
Given a model + id (or the currently pinned record from the view context), produce a short briefing the user can read in 30 seconds:
1. If model + id is missing, use the pinned record from `<ui_ctx>`. If still missing, call `ask_user` for the record reference. 2. Use `read_records` to fetch the record. Pass an explicit `fields` list scoped to the user-meaningful fields (skip technical or internal fields unless asked). 3. Output: - Header line: `Display Name (model,id)` - Up to 8 key/value bullets (label · value). - One-line state/lifecycle note ("draft", "in progress", "blocked by X"). - Top 3 most recent log notes from `mail.message` (skip auto/system) with author and date. 4. Stop. Do not propose actions unless asked.
Archive records after pre-confirming the impact with the user.

# Safe Archive
Archive records (`active = False`) only after explicit user confirmation, with a structured preview:
1. Resolve the target set: model + domain (or model + ids). If ambiguous, call `ask_user` once. 2. Use `search_count` to count the target set. If `> 50`, summarise that count and ask the user to confirm before listing. 3. Use `search_read` (limit 25) to fetch `id`, `display_name`, and any obviously linked counts (e.g. `sale_order_count`, `invoice_ids`). Show in a small table. 4. Call `ask_user` with `resolution='yesno'` and a structured `preview` of kind `update`, listing the targets and the `active: True → False` change. Stop. 5. On the user's "yes" answer (the next turn), call `update_records` to archive in one batch. Reply with one line: N records archived.
